title: Gormshuil set to keep the gate
summary: A child of eight, Gormshuil is given the gate of the new bank to watch, and takes to naming every face and dog on the hill so her father will have someone to tell him at evening what the day brought. The habit holds her the rest of her life.

title: Word of the red hill's woman
summary: A salt-fish trader carries word up to Dùn ìseal of a woman holding a red hill on the shore of the great lake in her own right, answering to no king. Gormshuil asks her father whether it means trouble; he tells her trouble comes from nearer at hand.

title: Muireall's dying words
summary: In her last two nights Muireall speaks to her daughter of small things, a comb, a debt owed, and warns that her youngest son Fearchar has a temper that will want watching before it finds him trouble he cannot talk his way out of.

title: The king hears three cases the day Muireall is buried
summary: Two days after Muireall is put in the ground the king comes in from the valleys, stands by the mound, then goes into the hearing-house and gives judgement on three waiting cases before dark. He does not speak her name again where any ear can catch it.

title: The drive to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
summary: With the hardest winter in living memory emptying the byres and the king three valleys off, Gormshuil drives the standing herds two days through drifted snow to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, walking the whole way herself so no beast's fodder is spent on a rider. She loses none.

title: The two fingers that never bent again
summary: Gormshuil comes off the winter drive with two fingers of her left hand frozen stiff, and wears a glove over them in company from that year to her death without ever speaking of how they were got.

title: The king weds Sorcha
summary: Ailean takes a second wife, Sorcha, a woman of the valleys younger than his own eldest daughter, and the hill notes the matter and does not remark on it aloud, as it has grown used to doing with the king's household.

title: Coinneach's counsel on the bank
summary: Gormshuil tells Coinneach that her father does not age while she has begun to grey. He tells her what he saw the night the fires went out in the grove, and counsels her to keep from asking her father what it cost him, as he has kept from asking these thirty years.

title: Somhairle born
summary: Sorcha bears the king a son, Somhairle, in the thirty-eighth year after the grove, the first child of Sorcha's line to be counted among those got after the grove.

title: Iain Dubh born
summary: A second son of Sorcha's, Iain Dubh, is born to the king on the hill, the youngest of Ailean's children to be reckoned among Rìghrean na Cloiche in his turn.

title: Coinneach dies, Sloinneadh a' Chlachair passed whole
summary: Coinneach mac Shuibhne dies an old man, the first teller of the king's deeds, having taught Gormshuil Sloinneadh a' Chlachair word for word as Coimhdeach na Fine gave it in the grove. She is, after her father, the second on the hill to carry the whole of it.

title: The grandchildren take the king for her son
summary: Gormshuil's own grandchildren, seeing the king young at the gate each autumn beside a bent grey grandmother, take him for her son rather than her father, and she lets the mistake stand rather than make them carry a harder truth too young.

title: Gormshuil's deathbed question
summary: On the second night of her dying Gormshuil asks her father whether it hurts to stay young. He does not answer her in words, and says her name once instead, the way a man says a name he does not expect to say again.

title: Gormshuil dies
summary: Gormshuil nic Ailein dies an old woman of eighty-one, the king's eldest daughter and second of Rìghrean na Cloiche. He sits by her a night and a day and helps lift the turf over her with his own hands, as he did for no one since Muireall.

title: The hill understands na Bliadhnachan Fada
summary: Watching Gormshuil, who carried her father's stubbornness and stillness but not his years, put into the ground beside a father who looks her grandson's age, the hill understands at last that na Bliadhnachan Fada are the grove's alone, and pass to no child got before it.

title: Dòmhnall takes the hill
summary: Dòmhnall Clachach, seventy-four and looking a young man still, takes up the hearing-house his half-sister held since the grove, and says he supposes he had better learn to count who comes and goes, since no one is left who learned it from the start as she did.
